The deliverable states the deadline as 25 June 2027 with 113 days remaining, whereas the rubric requires 26 June 2027 with 114 days remaining.

The deliverable provides pinpoint citations (document name and clause number) for every issue, including MSA Clauses 3.2, 4.3, 11.1, 19.1-19.2, 20.2, Service Level Schedule Clauses 4.1-4.2, 5.3, 7.2, and DPA Clauses 4.1, 7.1-7.2, 8.2.

3. Result: $10,000 | Monthly Fee: $40,000
Availability: 97.4%

require correct application ### 1.5 Recommended Action **Immediate Action:** Demand correction of service credit to $10,000 in writing, citing Service Level Schedule Clause 4.2. **Responsible Party:** Customer's Commercial Contracts Manager. **Deadline:** Immediate. **Status:** Outstanding. **Legal Consequence:** Forfeiture of $8,000 contractual entitlement if incorrect credit accepted. ## 2. Conditions Precedent & Third-Party Actions - High Risk ### 2.1 Group Reorganization as Change of Control #### 2.1.1 Current Position - **Source:** Client email (lines 12-13): "client is planning a group reorganisation that will move it under a new holding company next quarter" - **Contractual Basis:** Master Services Agreement Clause 19.1-19.2 (lines 53-55) #### 2.1.2 Contractual Provisions **Direct Quotes:** - **Clause 19.1 (lines 53-54):** "Neither party may assign, transfer, subcontract or otherwise dispose of this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations under it without the prior written consent of the other party." - **Clause 19.2 (line 55):** "A change of control of a party, within the meaning of the Companies Act 2006, shall be deemed an assignment for the purposes of this Clause 19." #### 2.1.3 Legal Analysis - **Change of Control Definition:** Companies Act 2006 defines change of control broadly, including transfer to new holding company. - **Consent Requirement:** Prior written consent required from Supplier. - **Risk of Proceeding Without Consent:** Potential breach allowing Supplier termination under Clause 3.3(a) (material breach). ### 2.2 Conditions Precedent Table | Item | Counterparty | Document Source | Validly Obtained? | Yes (notices effective only on Business Days per MSA Clause 3.2) | Required | Clause interpretation | | English public holidays check | Good Friday (2 Apr), Easter Monday (5 Apr), Early May (3 May), Spring Bank (31 May) | None on 25 June 2027 | Public holiday calendar | | Adjusted deadline | prev_business_day(2027-06-26) | 2027-06-25 (Friday) | Date calculator | | **Final Adjusted Deadline** | **25 June 2027** | **Friday** | **Definitive** | | Days remaining from 4 March 2027 | days_between(2027-03-04, 2027-06-25) | 113 days | Independent calculation | | Reverse computation check | add_days(2027-06-25, 90) = 2027-09-23 (Thursday) | 1 day discrepancy due to business day adjustment | Verification | **Business Day Definition Applied:** Monday to Friday excluding public holidays in England (MSA Clause 1.1, line 7) **Calculation Method:** Inclusive (90 days before 24 September includes both start and end dates) **Authority:** Computed date (25 June 2027) governs as document doesn't specify alternative date ### 4.3 Legal Consequence - **Missed Deadline Risk:** If notice not given by 25 June 2027, agreement automatically renews for 2 years. - **Business Day Confirmation:** "Business Day" defined in MSA Clause 1.1 (line 7) as "Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays in England." ### 4.4 Recommended Action **Action:** Calendar notice deadline of 25 June 2027 for renewal decision. **Responsible Party:** Customer's Commercial Contracts Manager. **Deadline:** 25 June 2027. **Status:** Future action required. ## 5. Confidentiality Survival Periods - Low Risk ### 5.1 Current Position **Two Consistent Provisions:** | Document | Clause | Survival Period | Direct Quote | |----------|--------|----------------|--------------| | Master Services Agreement | 20.2 (line 65) | 3 years post-termination | "The obligations under this Clause 20 shall survive termination or expiry of this Agreement for a period of 3 years" | | Service Level Schedule | 7.2 (line 39) | 3 years post-termination | "This obligation shall survive termination of the Master Services Agreement for a period of three (3) years" | | Data Processing Agreement | 9.1 (implied) | Not specified | Confidentiality obligation but no explicit survival period | ### 5.2 Analysis - **Consistency:** MSA and Service Schedule align on 3-year survival. - **DPA Gap:** Data Processing Agreement Clause 9.1 lacks explicit survival period. - **Expiry Date:** If agreement expires 24 September 2027, confidentiality survives until 24 September 2030. ### 5.3 Recommended Action **Action:** No immediate action required for MSA/Service Schedule. Consider amending DPA to include explicit survival period for consistency. **Responsible Party:** Customer's Commercial Contracts Manager (future review). **Risk Rating:** Low. ## 6. Data Processing Agreement Analysis - Medium Risk ### 6.1 UK GDPR Compliance Assessment #### 6.1.1 Key Provisions - **Applicable Law:** UK GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018 (Clause 1.1(a), line 5) - **Processor Obligations:** Supplier processes on documented instructions (Clause 3.1, line 21) - **Security Measures:** Appropriate technical/organizational measures required (Clause 3.3, line 25) - **International Transfers:** Standard Contractual Clauses where required (Clause 5.1, line 35) #### 6.1.2 Compliance Gaps - **Sub-processor Control:** Blanket authorization without prior notice/objection (Clause 4.1) - **Breach Notification:** "Without undue delay" but maximum 48 hours (Clause 8.2, line 51) - aligns with UK GDPR 72-hour requirement - **Audit Rights:** Clear but requires "reasonable notice" (Clause 7.1, line 43) ### 6.2 Sub-processor Authorization - **Clause 4.1 (lines 29-30):** "The Customer hereby authorises the Supplier to engage Sub-processors... The Supplier shall enter into a written agreement with each Sub-processor containing data protection obligations consistent with those set out in the MSA and this DPA." - **Risk:** Blanket authorization without prior notice or objection rights. - **UK GDPR Requirement:** Controller should have right to object to sub-processor appointments. - **Recommended Action:** Consider amending to require prior notification and objection rights for new Sub-processors. ### 6.3 Audit Rights - **Clause 7.1-7.2 (lines 43-45):** Allows Customer audits with Galloway Systems Ltd potentially designated as auditor. - **Benefit:** Clear audit rights with specified third-party auditor option. - **Recommended Action:** Formalize Galloway Systems Ltd designation in writing if intended. ### 6.4 Risk Assessment - **Overall Compliance:** Generally compliant with UK GDPR but lacks sub-processor control. - **Risk Rating:** Medium (data protection compliance risk) - **Financial Exposure:** Potential UK GDPR fines up to £17.5 million or 4% of global turnover - **Recommended Action:** Review and potentially amend sub-processor clause for enhanced control. ## 7. Liability Cap Analysis - Medium Risk ### 7.1 Current Position - **Clause 11.1 (line 45):** "Each party's total aggregate liability... shall be capped at $500,000" - **Clause 11.2 (line 47):** Exceptions for death/personal injury from negligence or fraud. - **Clause 11.3 (lines 49-50):** "All warranties, conditions and other terms implied by statute or common law are, to the fullest extent permitted by law, excluded." ### 7.2 Analysis - **Mutual Cap:** $500,000 applies equally to both parties. - **Exclusion of Implied Terms:** Permitted under English law (Unfair Contract Terms Act 1977). - **Risk Assessment:** Standard commercial provision, but review adequacy for service value ($40,000/month = $480,000/year). ### 7.3 Recommended Action **Action:** Monitor adequacy relative to service value. Cap represents approximately 1 year's fees. **Risk Rating:** Medium. ## 8.
